questions.explanation: k-Means minimises WCSS — the total squared Euclidean distance from each observation to its cluster centroid. Minimising WCSS creates compact, internally cohesive clusters.

questions.text: Why should nstart be set to 25 (or higher) in kmeans()?
options: Because k-Means converges to a local minimum; multiple random starts increases the chance of finding the global minimum
To run the algorithm for exactly 25 iterations
questions.explanation: k-Means converges to a local minimum depending on the random initialisation. Running nstart = 25 starts means 25 random initialisations are tried; the best result (lowest WCSS) is returned.

questions.text: The elbow plot shows silhouette scores on the y-axis.
questions.explanation: The elbow plot shows WCSS (total within-cluster sum of squares) on the y-axis against the number of clusters k. The silhouette plot is a separate diagnostic that shows average silhouette width against k.

questions.text: The silhouette score for an observation ranges from -1 to +1. A score close to +1 means:
options: The observation is likely an outlier
The observation is well-matched to its cluster and poorly matched to neighbouring clusters
The observation belongs equally to two clusters
questions.explanation: A silhouette close to +1 indicates the observation is much closer to its own cluster centroid than to the nearest other cluster. A score near 0 indicates borderline assignment; negative scores suggest possible misassignment.

questions.text: After clustering policyholders, you want to describe each cluster in business terms. What is the appropriate next step?
options: Re-run k-means with a different random seed
Join cluster labels back to the original data and compute per-cluster summaries of key variables
Remove the smallest cluster because it may be noise
Increase k until each cluster has exactly one member
questions.explanation: Cluster profiling involves joining the integer cluster labels back to the original (unscaled) data and computing group-level summaries (means, proportions). This translates the abstract cluster numbers into interpretable business segments.
